steps.title: Reproduction and Hormones
steps.body: The menstrual cycle is controlled by four main hormones. These hormones can be used in contraception and in fertility treatments such as IVF.

steps.title: The menstrual cycle
steps.body: is a roughly 28-day cycle in which an egg is released from an ovary and the uterus lining is prepared for a possible pregnancy. If the egg is not fertilised, the uterus lining breaks down (menstruation/period).

steps.title: Hormone interactions
steps.body: FSH stimulates oestrogen production Oestrogen inhibits FSH (negative feedback) and stimulates LH LH triggers ovulation Progesterone inhibits both FSH and LH If progesterone levels fall (no pregnancy), the uterus lining breaks down and the cycle restarts

steps.title: Contraception
steps.body: prevents pregnancy by preventing ovulation, preventing fertilisation, or preventing implantation of a fertilised egg.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn all four hormones, where they are produced, and what they do — this is very commonly tested FSH and LH are produced by the PITUITARY GLAND; oestrogen and progesterone by the OVARIES Remember: oestrogen INHIBITS FSH; progesterone INHIBITS FSH and LH — these are negative feedback When asked about contraception, explain HOW it works at a hormonal level (not just "it prevents pregnancy") For IVF, always mention FSH and LH at the start to stimulate superovulation Don't confuse FSH with LH: FSH matures the egg, LH triggers ovulation (release) When discussing ethical issues, give balanced points and explain both sides The "in vitro" in IVF means "in glass" (in the lab), not inside the body
